capture.final_message:
Use level-set characterizations of semicontinuity throughout.

- For the first conjunct, for every threshold \(c\),
  \[
  \{x\in s\mid \inf_i f_i(x)<c\}
  =\bigcup_i\{x\in s\mid f_i(x)<c\}.
  \]
  Each set on the right is relatively open in \(s\) by upper semicontinuity of \(f_i\), so the union is relatively open. The complete linear order supplies the needed characterization of strict inequality against an arbitrary infimum, including the empty-index case.

- Prove both sides of the displayed `Iff` independently. For the indicator claim, use \(y\le 0\) to classify its strict upper-level sets: depending on the threshold, they are either empty, the whole space, or the complement of the closed set \(s\). Hence the indicator is lower semicontinuous.

- For the compactness claim, rewrite the empty intersection as
  \[
  \forall x\in s,\ \exists i\in I,\quad c<f_i(x).
  \]
  Lower semicontinuity on \(s\) makes the sets
  \[
  U_i=\{x\in s\mid c<f_i(x)\}
  \]
  relatively open. They cover the compact set \(s\), so compactness gives a finite subcover. Record its indices as a finset of the subtype \(I\), which is exactly the right-hand statement. Conversely, a finite family with the stated pointwise property immediately rules out any point in the intersection.
